content.text: Pending response to code review comments.
This is on hold pending an update to Jena to fix an issue with loading the Fuseki config file.  See
– there is a commit addressing this problem, so we'll need to wait for the next release to proceed.
JENA-915 has been resolved. Now waiting on a 2.0.1 release.
Since we are slowly moving away from Tomcat, does this matter any more? I'm more than happy to have it closed if others feel the same way.

Are we moving away from Tomcat?  To Jetty?  I believe part of the motivation for this ticket was to allow access control via the servlet container (which isn't supported in standalone mode), so I still think it's worth switching from standalone to war-based deployment for that.
I was referring to OSGi'fying most of the stack. Good to know that this is still relevant than.
Fuseki 2.3.0 is out, so I can try and tackle it later on this week if y'all want.
Needs review, and testing. One note, you have to wait about 20-30 seconds for the test dataset to get itself loaded and setup after Tomcat starts.
Fuseki deploys, which is great. However, the camel-toolbox needs to be configured to talk to the new Fuseki location.
You can verify that your update works or not by adding a resource to F4 and querying Fuseki. You should see both the new resource as well as the audit entry.

Yeah, we need to update the ports to 3030 at minimum. I'll configure that locally after vagrant builds, and verify. If that does the job, shall I do a pull request for fcrepo-camel-toolbox as well, since they'll need to be changed at the same time for the issue?
Updated fcrepo-camel-toolbox, built, and deployed artifact on vagrant VM. I added a new object and was successful.

fields.summary: fcrepo4-vagrant: Move Fuseki install from stand alone server to deployable war

comments.body: Responded

This is on hold pending an update to Jena to fix an issue with loading the Fuseki config file. See https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/JENA-915 – there is a commit addressing this problem, so we'll need to wait for the next release to proceed.
JENA-915 has been resolved. Now waiting on a 2.0.1 release.
Since we are slowly moving away from Tomcat, does this matter any more? I'm more than happy to have it closed if others feel the same way.

Are we moving away from Tomcat? To Jetty? I believe part of the motivation for this ticket was to allow access control via the servlet container (which isn't supported in standalone mode), so I still think it's worth switching from standalone to war-based deployment for that.

Good point Former user!

I was referring to OSGi'fying most of the stack. Good to know that this is still relevant than.

Fuseki 2.3.0 is out, so I can try and tackle it later on this week if y'all want.

Second pull request: https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo4-vagrant/pull/18

Needs review, and testing. One note, you have to wait about 20-30 seconds for the test dataset to get itself loaded and setup after Tomcat starts.

Fuseki deploys, which is great. However, the camel-toolbox needs to be configured to talk to the new Fuseki location.
See: https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-camel-toolbox/tree/master/fcrepo-indexing-triplestore#configuration
and
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-camel-toolbox/tree/master/fcrepo-audit-triplestore#configuration

You can verify that your update works or not by adding a resource to F4 and querying Fuseki. You should see both the new resource as well as the audit entry.

Yeah, we need to update the ports to 3030 at minimum. I'll configure that locally after vagrant builds, and verify. If that does the job, shall I do a pull request for fcrepo-camel-toolbox as well, since they'll need to be changed at the same time for the issue?

Updated fcrepo-camel-toolbox, built, and deployed artifact on vagrant VM. I added a new object and was successful.
